name: Autoimmune Neurological Channelopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Autoimmune Neurological Channelopathy

criteria.description: Presence of fluctuating neurological symptoms consistent with channelopathy (e.g., episodic weakness, sensory disturbances)
Detection of specific autoantibodies against neuronal ion channels in serum or CSF
Electrophysiological studies demonstrating abnormal nerve excitability or conduction consistent with channel dysfunction
Exclusion of alternative diagnoses such as genetic channelopathies or metabolic neuropathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fluctuating neurological symptoms plus detection of specific autoantibodies and supportive electrophysiological evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, serological, and electrophysiological data; genetic testing recommended to exclude hereditary channelopathies

pathognomonic.symptomName: Episodic muscle weakness with rapid onset and remission
searchTerms: muscle weakness that comes and goes quickly

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fasciculations and muscle cramps linked to ion channel autoimmunity
searchTerms: muscle twitching and cramps from immune causes

common.symptomName: Sensory disturbances including paresthesia and numbness
searchTerms: abnormal skin feelings like pins and needles

common.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction such as orthostatic hypotension
searchTerms: autonomic nervous system problems causing low blood pressure

common.symptomName: Fatigable muscle weakness exacerbated by activity

searchTerms: cranial nerve problems causing vision issues

occasional.symptomName: Mild autonomic symptoms such as dry mouth
searchTerms: dry mouth and mild autonomic symptoms
seizures caused by nerve channel problems
epileptic fits linked to ion channel dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to autonomic involvement
searchTerms: heart rhythm issues due to autonomic dysfunction
cardiac arrhythmias related to nerve involvement

laboratory: Presence of autoantibodies against voltage-gated potassium channels (VGKC), voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCC), or other neuronal ion channels
Elevated inflammatory markers in CSF (mild pleocytosis, elevated protein)
imaging: MRI brain and spinal cord typically normal or showing nonspecific inflammatory changes
Nerve conduction studies showing abnormal excitability or neuromyotonia
genetic: Negative for known hereditary channelopathy mutations (e.g., SCN4A, CACNA1A)
other: Positive response to immunotherapy (IVIG, steroids, plasmapheresis)
Electromyography demonstrating spontaneous muscle fiber activity

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutation confirmed by molecular testing
Usually earlier onset and family history
Demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies
Absence of specific neuronal ion channel autoantibodies

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
New onset seizures or altered mental status
Failure to respond to standard immunotherapy
references: Lancaster E. Autoimmune channelopathies of the nervous system. Nat Rev Neurol. 2016;12(2):86-99.
Vincent A, et al. Autoimmune channelopathies: clinical features and immunopathogenesis. Lancet Neurol. 2010;9(6): 565-577.
